title: Quiet reserve suppression during AZ surge leading to customer throttles
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a regional traffic surge in eu-west-1, a subset of tenants experienced silent capacity denials from reserved pools. Requests were admitted by the routing layer but later dropped by the reserve allocator without clear errors surfaced to customers. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, hotfixes, and customer comms for the event.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-19 23:40 UTC and 2026-02-20 03:12 UTC several mid-market customers saw increased 429s and elevated latencies for reserved-pool-backed Dedicated deployments. Affected tenants lost burst headroom and briefly fell back to lower-throughput pools, causing failed SLAs for high-priority payment flows at two customers.
timeline: 2026-02-19 23:30 UTC - surge begins in eu-west-1; 23:45 - ops alert: spike in admission rejections for reserved allocator; 00:05 - telemetry shows allocator lease queue growth and per-tenant reserve counters dropping; 00:22 - on-call applied emergency admission-relax patch (rollout 00:24) to allow transient oversubscribe; 01:10 - observed heatmap showed recovery for most tenants but two customers remained rate-limited; 03:00 - hotfix merged to fix lease-table TTL bug and rolled out to eu-west-1; 03:12 - metrics normalized and customer 429s subsided.
root_cause: A cascade of three interacting issues: 1) A regression in the lease table TTL introduced in release dedicated-autoscaler-2026.02 caused stale lease entries to persist longer than expected under high churn. 2) The weighted capacity calculator underestimated effective headroom for heterogeneous GPU families in the affected AZ, causing the allocator to view the reserved pool as 'full' sooner. 3) Admission gating was strict when the allocator perceived high utilization, returning silent denials upstream rather than explicit reject codes, which hid the failure mode from routing-level dashboards.
temporary_mitigation: Rolled back strict admission policy to an emergency oversubscribe mode for eu-west-1 to reduce customer 429s. Deployed a short-lived background sweep to trim stale leases older than the intended TTL. Opened prioritized support threads to impacted customers with tailored traffic rerouting guidance and temporary quota increases where safe.
permanent_fix: Patch 1: Correct TTL computation in lease table and add defensive expiry backfill job. Patch 2: Rework weighted capacity model to use per-GPU performance profiles and active sequence-length distribution, not just nominal vCPU/GPU ratios. Patch 3: Change allocator admission path to emit explicit mismatch metrics and fail open for short-lived spikes, plus a feature-flagged gradual degrade behavior rather than immediate hard denials.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with 10% traffic (controlled by rollout knob) for 2 hours; monitor allocator admission rate, lease-table GC rate, and customer 4xx rates. If stable, expand to 50% for 1 hour, then full region. Staged rollouts for us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 to follow next maintenance window. Backout steps are pre-recorded and tested in staging.
test_plan: Unit tests for TTL edge cases and lease GC. Integration test harness to simulate churned lease insert/delete under mixed GPU shapes. Load test that reproduces surge profile (90th-99th percentile sequences) to validate admission path and slow-path recovery. Post-deploy smoke that asserts no silent denials by checking explicit admission metrics and upstream routing errors.
monitoring_and_alerts: New alerts: sustained allocator lease-table growth > 5k entries for 10m; weighted-headroom delta > 10% between estimator and actual free slots; silent-denials count > 1% of total admissions. Dashboards added: per-AZ headroom estimate vs observed, lease TTL distribution histogram, and customer-facing 4xx trending by reserved-pool tag.
postmortem_notes: Root cause was systemic: a minor TTL miscompute had outsized effect under churn because of a prior optimization that removed periodic GC runs. The weighted capacity model had been acceptable for stable traffic but lacked sensitivity to short sequence-length bursts common in this customer cohort. Communication gaps: routing teams did not surface admission-level rejects because the allocator's internal path returned soft failures. Learnings: prioritize end-to-end observability for admission flows and avoid silent failure modes.

resolution: Merged TTL and weighted-capacity fixes (PR #1287). Canary in eu-west-1 completed without regression. Monitoring alerts added and runbook updated. Customer follow-ups completed; offers for SLA credit being handled by account teams.
notes_for_follow_up: 1) Add periodic chaos tests for allocator lease churn. 2) Audit all admission paths for silent-fail patterns. 3) Expand GPU perf profiling dataset to cover new cloud instance types. 4) Schedule a post-incident blameless review with routing, allocator, and console teams.
communication_plan: PM to send consolidated incident summary to impacted customers by 2026-03-07. Support to escalate any remaining SLA credit requests to finance. Internal debrief scheduled for 2026-03-09.
next_steps: Complete rollout to other regions, finish performance profiler data collection, close related follow-up tickets, and incorporate findings into autoscaler roadmap.
